source_trace.title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve Board finalizes rules that tailor its regulations for domestic and foreign banks to more closely match their risk profiles

impact_scope_evidence.quote: The rules reduce compliance requirements for firms with less risk while maintaining the most stringent requirements for the largest and most complex banks.
impact_scope_evidence.rationale: The rules are specifically tailored to banks, adjusting their regulatory requirements based on their risk profiles, which indicates an industry-wide impact on the banking sector.

impact_scope_evidence.quote: The rules do not reduce capital or liquidity requirements for firms in the highest risk categories, including U.S.
impact_scope_evidence.rationale: The rules affect the broader financial system and economy by altering capital and liquidity requirements for banks, which has implications for the overall market.

events.quote: Federal Reserve Board finalizes rules that tailor its regulations for domestic and foreign banks to more closely match their risk profiles
The rules build on the Board's existing practice of tailoring its requirements and are consistent with changes made by the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief, and Consumer Protecti
The Board estimates that the changes in the aggregate will result in a 0.6 percent decrease in required capital and a reduction of 2 percent of required liquid assets for all banks
The regulatory capital and liquidity aspects of the rules were jointly developed with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
The rules will be effective 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.
